title: Risk review is deadlined ahead of strategic scope approval so business decisions cannot be made before risk findings
content:
A.1.10.2.3.2.2.3.1.2 requires that both the Executive Process Liaison's delivery of items and the Core Council Risk Advisor's pre-risk review "be completed by Wednesday, 16:00 UTC of week 0 **so that the Strategic Team's scope approval that follows is informed by the Core Council Risk Advisor's findings**."

A.1.10.2.3.2.2.3.1.2.2 restates the dependency, and A.1.10.2.3.2.2.3.1.3 puts the Strategic Team's approval — which "reflects the Strategic Team's assessment of business needs and strategic alignment" — at the end of Friday, after the risk input has landed.

The rare thing here is that the Atlas states the *reason* for a deadline rather than only the deadline. That converts a scheduling detail into a governance control: risk assessment cannot become a post-hoc justification for a commitment already made on strategic grounds.

The ordering matters because the failure mode it blocks is invisible in the artifacts. A strategy-first process still produces a risk review, a signed proposal, and a compliant paper trail — it just produces them in the order where the review can no longer change the outcome. Sequencing is the only way to prevent that, and it only works if the sequence is enforced as a rule rather than treated as a convention.
description: Both land Wednesday 16:00 UTC of week 0, with the stated purpose that the Strategic Team's approval is informed by the Risk Advisor — the ordering, not the scheduling, is the control.
